review_rationale: Selected because the country-food signal is CONSISTENTLY_HIGH across all six model scenarios and observed soybean imports are highly concentrated in one immediate trade partner.
approved_narrative_scope: Use as a country-level example of stable import vulnerability combined with high observed supplier concentration. The United States represented approximately 97% of pooled observed supplier share for this analytical scope during 2021-2023.
additional_limitations: Observed supplier relationships represent immediate trade partners, not agricultural origin. Do not interpret static removal results as a prediction of food shortage or disruption.

review_rationale: Selected because the palm-oil country-food signal is CONSISTENTLY_HIGH across all six scenarios and the dominant observed supplier is also part of a strong systemic supplier-food signal.
approved_narrative_scope: Use to connect country-level vulnerability with broader supplier-network reach. Indonesia represented approximately 71% of Oman's pooled observed supplier share for this palm-oil scope during 2021-2023.
additional_limitations: Gross import reliance can exceed 100% because the metric uses the FBS domestic-supply denominator and may reflect trade, processing, re-export, or accounting structure. Do not interpret the ratio as a literal percent of consumption supplied by imports.

review_rationale: Selected because the country-food signal is CONSISTENTLY_HIGH across all six scenarios and the dominant observed supplier is itself a CONSISTENT_SYSTEMIC_SIGNAL supplier-food node.
approved_narrative_scope: Use alongside Oman to show that palm-oil vulnerability can connect multiple importers to systemically important supplier-food nodes. Malaysia represented approximately 80% of Türkiye's pooled observed supplier share for this scope during 2021-2023.
additional_limitations: Supplier is an observed immediate trade partner, not necessarily the agricultural origin. Static removal tests do not model substitution or behavioral response.

review_rationale: Selected as a clear and interpretable example of extreme observed supplier concentration with a CONSISTENTLY_HIGH country-food signal across all six model scenarios.
approved_narrative_scope: Use as an intuitive country-level concentration example. New Zealand represented approximately 99% of pooled observed supplier share for Samoa's onion analytical scope during 2021-2023.
additional_limitations: The analysis describes the observed trade network only. It does not model inventory, domestic substitutes, alternative suppliers, prices, logistics, or policy response.

review_rationale: Selected because the supplier-food node is a CONSISTENT_SYSTEMIC_SIGNAL near the top of the within-scope systemic distribution and has broad observed importer reach.
approved_narrative_scope: Use as one half of the palm-oil systemic concentration story. Indonesia is observed across 78 importer networks for this analytical scope, including 17 importers with elevated country-food signals. Across static removal tests, 101 observed importer-year edges lost more than 50% of their recorded supplier share when Indonesia was removed.
additional_limitations: Removal tests are static diagnostics only. No supplier substitution, inventory, rerouting, price response, domestic production response, or policy intervention is modeled.

review_rationale: Selected because the supplier-food node is a CONSISTENT_SYSTEMIC_SIGNAL near the top of the within-scope systemic distribution and complements the Indonesia palm-oil result.
approved_narrative_scope: Use together with Indonesia to illustrate systemic concentration in the observed palm-oil trade network. Malaysia is observed across 76 importer networks for this scope, including 17 importers with elevated country-food signals. In 94 static removal tests, the removed supplier share exceeded 50%.
additional_limitations: Observed exporter relationships do not establish agricultural origin. Removal results describe the recorded network and are not disruption forecasts.

review_rationale: Selected because the supplier-food node is a CONSISTENT_SYSTEMIC_SIGNAL and links the highly concentrated Samoa case to a broader importer network.
approved_narrative_scope: Use with the Samoa example to distinguish bilateral concentration from supplier-network reach. New Zealand is observed supplying this onion scope to 32 importers, including 13 with elevated analytical signals.
additional_limitations: Importer count measures observed network breadth, not the number of countries predicted to experience disruption.

review_rationale: Selected because the supplier-food node is a CONSISTENT_SYSTEMIC_SIGNAL with an average systemic percentile of 1.00 and observed relationships with 58 importers.
approved_narrative_scope: Use as a supplier-network example connected to the Costa Rica soybean case. Twelve connected importers have elevated country-food signals. Static removal tests also include three importer-food-year networks where removing the U.S. edge left no other observed supplier.
additional_limitations: The three zero-remaining-supplier observations refer only to the observed network in the dataset. They do not imply that those importers would have no soybean supply after an actual disruption.
